entities.name: Caroline
entities.description: A transgender woman who began transitioning around 2020 and speaks openly about it. Originally from Sweden, she moved away around 2019 and has known her present circle of friends since then. Over 2023 she went from attending an LGBTQ support group to speaking at a school, mentoring LGBTQ youth, joining the activist group Connected LGBTQ Activists and volunteering at an LGBTQ+ youth centre. She is pursuing a career in counselling and mental health, passed her adoption agency interviews on 20 October 2023, paints and draws, plays acoustic guitar and keeps a guinea pig called Oscar. Melanie calls her Caro.

entities.name: Melanie
entities.description: A married mother of several children and Caroline's friend. She has made art for about seven years and counts painting and pottery as her two muses; she signed up for a pottery class in July 2023 and had to break from it after an injury in September 2023. She also runs, plays the clarinet and the violin, camps and hikes with her family, volunteers with them at a homeless shelter, and keeps a dog, Oliver, and two cats, Luna and Bailey. Caroline calls her Mel.

entities.name: Melanie's children
entities.description: Melanie's children, referred to throughout as 'the kids', 'my fam' and individually as her son, her daughter and her youngest. They go camping, hiking and to the beach with her, made pots at a pottery workshop in July 2023, and her son was in a road accident during the family road trip of 14-15 October 2023 and was unhurt. Recorded as one subject because the conversation almost always speaks of them together.

entities.name: Melanie's husband
entities.description: Melanie's husband, also called her partner. They married around 2018, five years before June 2023, at a wedding Melanie remembers for its flowers and for the promise to be together forever. He appears in her family photographs and supported her through her move.

entities.name: Caroline's grandmother
entities.description: Caroline's grandmother in Sweden, who gave her a cross-and-heart necklace when she was young as a symbol of love, faith and strength.

entities.name: Sweden
entities.description: Caroline's home country, where her grandmother lives. She moved away from it around 2019, four years before June 2023, and speaks of the necklace her grandmother gave her as a reminder of her roots there.

entities.name: the LGBTQ support group
entities.description: The LGBTQ support group Caroline attended on 7 May 2023, where transgender people shared their stories. She said it made her feel accepted and gave her the courage to embrace herself, and it is part of why she wants to work in counselling.

entities.name: the LGBTQ-inclusive adoption agency
entities.description: The adoption agency Caroline chose in May 2023 because it helps LGBTQ+ people adopt. She spoke of it as one agency she was looking into, then of applying to 'adoption agencies' in August 2023 and passing 'the adoption agency interviews' on 20 October 2023; the three mentions are joined here as one body because nothing distinguishes them.

entities.name: Melanie's pottery class
entities.description: The pottery class Melanie signed up for on 2 July 2023. She made a black-and-white flower-patterned bowl there, and a flower-decorated plate on 24 August 2023. An injury in September 2023 forced a break from it.

entities.name: Charlotte's Web
entities.description: The book Melanie loved as a child, which she says showed her how friendship and compassion can make a difference.

entities.name: Becoming Nicole
entities.description: Becoming Nicole by Amy Ellis Nutt, the true story of a transgender girl and her family. Caroline's favourite book and one she recommends: she says it made her feel connected, gave her hope for her own path, and taught her self-acceptance and how to find support.

entities.name: Caroline's cross-and-heart necklace
entities.description: A necklace with a cross and a heart that Caroline's grandmother in Sweden gave her when she was young. Caroline treasures it as standing for love, faith and strength and as a reminder of her roots and her family's support.

entities.name: Caroline's hand-painted bowl
entities.description: A hand-painted bowl a friend made for Caroline's 18th birthday around 2013. She keeps it for its pattern and colours and as a reminder of art and self-expression.

entities.name: painting and drawing
entities.description: The art both women make. Melanie has painted for about seven years, favours landscapes, still life and animals, and paints with her children. Caroline has made art since she was about 17 and uses painting and drawing to express her trans experience, explore her gender identity and advocate for the LGBTQ+ community; her work includes 'Embracing Identity', a self-portrait with a blue face, a red-and-blue piece about the binary gender system, and a stained glass window for a local church.

entities.name: pottery
entities.description: Melanie's craft, which she calls therapy rather than a hobby and says helps her express her emotions. She took it up with a class on 2 July 2023, has made bowls and a plate, took her children to a pottery workshop, and broke from it after an injury in September 2023. Caroline had still not tried it as of September 2023.

entities.name: running
entities.description: Melanie's way of destressing and clearing her mind. It started as part of the daily time she carved out for herself in May 2023, grew to longer distances by July 2023 when she bought new running shoes, and she credits it with improving her mental health. She also ran a charity race for mental health on 20 May 2023.

entities.name: reading
entities.description: Reading matters to both of them. Caroline says books guide and motivate her and are a big part of her journey, and she is stocking a children's library for the child she hopes to adopt. Melanie reads as part of her daily me-time and kept reading a book Caroline recommended while she was injured.

entities.name: hiking
entities.description: Melanie's family hike in the mountains and explore forests on their camping trips, and she walked a trail with the children on 19 October 2023. Caroline also hikes; it was on a hike shortly before 17 August 2023 that she met a group of religious conservatives who upset her.

entities.name: camping
entities.description: The family tradition Melanie calls the highlight of their summer: marshmallows, campfire stories and nature. Trips mentioned include the mountains in June 2023, a weekend on 8-9 July 2023, the beach, the forest, one a few weeks before September 2023, and the 2022 trip on which they watched the Perseid meteor shower.

entities.name: Caroline's LGBTQ advocacy
entities.description: Caroline's ongoing work for the LGBTQ+ and trans community: speaking at a school in June 2023, attending pride parades, an LGBTQ conference and a transgender poetry reading, mentoring LGBTQ youth, joining Connected LGBTQ Activists, volunteering at an LGBTQ+ youth centre and using her art to argue for acceptance.

entities.name: Caroline's gender transition
entities.description: Caroline's transition as a transgender woman, begun around 2020. She refers to it as 'my transition', 'my journey' and 'coming out'. Friends, family and mentors supported her through it, though some friends could not handle it; art helped her explore her changing body and identity, and she says the best part has been realising she can be herself without fear.

entities.name: Caroline's adoption
entities.description: Caroline's plan to adopt as a single parent, which she calls a lifelong dream. She was researching LGBTQ-friendly agencies in May 2023, attended an adoption council meeting on 14 July 2023 and an adoption advice group, applied to agencies in the week to 23 August 2023, contacted her mentor for advice on 13 October 2023 and passed the agency interviews on 20 October 2023.

entities.name: Caroline's counselling and mental health career
entities.description: Caroline's plan to train for and work in counselling or mental health, so she can support people who have been through what she has. It narrowed over 2023 from 'continuing my education and exploring career options' to working specifically with transgender people on self-acceptance and mental health, after an LGBTQ+ counselling workshop on 23 June 2023.

entities.name: Caroline's children's library
entities.description: The library of children's books Caroline is building for when she has children through adoption: classics, stories from different cultures and educational books. She looks forward to reading to them.

entities.name: Oliver
entities.description: Melanie's dog, one of the household's pets along with the cat Luna; a second cat, Bailey, joined them by August 2023. Melanie says he once hid his bone in her slipper.

entities.name: Luna
entities.description: Melanie's cat, one of the household's pets along with the dog Oliver; a second cat, Bailey, joined them by August 2023. Melanie says the pets brighten the family's day.

entities.name: Matt Patterson
entities.description: The musician whose concert Melanie and her family attended on 13 August 2023 for her daughter's birthday. Melanie called him very talented and praised his voice and songs.

entities.name: Connected LGBTQ Activists
entities.description: The LGBTQ activist group Caroline joined on 18 July 2023. It is made up of all kinds of people working for positive change, holds regular meetings and plans events and campaigns; Caroline says it gives her a platform to use her voice.

entities.name: the LGBTQ youth mentorship programme
entities.description: The mentorship programme for LGBTQ youth that Caroline joined over the weekend of 15-16 July 2023. She mentors a transgender teenager, working with them on confidence and coping strategies, and the two attended an LGBT pride event together in June 2023.

entities.name: the LGBTQ+ youth centre
entities.description: The LGBTQ+ youth centre Caroline volunteers at, talking to young people facing what she faced and sharing her own story. She also referred in July 2023 to visiting 'a LGBTQ center' which inspired a painting about unity and strength; the two mentions are joined here as one place because nothing in the conversation separates them. As of August 2023 she and the centre were putting together a talent show for the young people.

entities.name: Caroline's LGBTQ art show
entities.description: An art show of LGBTQ artists that Caroline is putting together and at which she will exhibit her paintings. She described it in July 2023 as happening the following month and in August 2023 as happening the following month again; she intends it to spread understanding and acceptance.

entities.name: Bailey
entities.description: Melanie's second cat, which the household had acquired by 23 August 2023, joining the dog Oliver and the cat Luna.

entities.name: Oscar
entities.description: Caroline's guinea pig, whom she describes as great company. His favourite food is parsley and vegetables generally.

entities.name: the Grand Canyon
entities.description: The place Melanie's children enjoyed on the family road trip of 14-15 October 2023, the trip on which her son was in an accident.

entities.name: Summer Sounds
entities.description: The band Melanie saw play an outdoor show before 28 August 2023. She says they played a lively pop song that got everyone dancing and singing, and that it reminded her how music brings people together.

entities.name: Brave
entities.description: 'Brave' by Sara Bareilles, the song Caroline says has the most significance for her. She reads it as being about courage and fighting for what is right, and it makes her think of the paths she has taken and the progress she has made.

entities.name: playing the guitar
entities.description: Caroline took up the acoustic guitar around 2018, about five years before August 2023. She says playing it helps her get her emotions out, express herself and escape into her feelings.

entities.name: playing the clarinet
entities.description: Melanie has played the clarinet since she was young and says it is a way to express herself and relax.

claims.text: Caroline painted a sunset after visiting the beach in the week before 25 August 2023, wanting to capture how amazing and calming she found the sun dipping below the horizon.
claims.speaker: Caroline

claims.text: Melanie spent 24 August 2023 volunteering with her family at a homeless shelter; she found it hard to see people so neglected but felt they had made a difference.
claims.speaker: Melanie

claims.text: Caroline said that finding a community where she is accepted, loved and supported is what mattered most in her decision to transition and join the transgender community.
claims.speaker: Caroline

claims.text: A mural of a rainbow flag with an eagle is important to Caroline: she reads the flag as the courage and strength of the trans community and the eagle as freedom and pride, representing her own resilience.
claims.speaker: Caroline

claims.text: Caroline made a stained glass window for a local church showing time changing people's lives, which she meant to represent her own journey as a transgender woman and the acceptance of growth and change; she said it is also a symbol of togetherness and celebrating differences.
claims.speaker: Caroline

claims.text: Caroline came across a rainbow-painted sidewalk laid for Pride Month while walking in her neighbourhood and photographed it, saying it showed that love and acceptance can be found even where least expected.
claims.speaker: Caroline

claims.text: Caroline said art lifts her mood and lets her show her feelings and capture beautiful moments, and that drawing flowers is one of her favourite things to do.
claims.speaker: Caroline

claims.text: Melanie said landscapes and still life are her favourite subjects to paint, and that she was planning several autumn-inspired paintings.
claims.speaker: Melanie

claims.text: On 25 August 2023 Caroline said she was organising an LGBTQ art show for the following month featuring LGBTQ artists, at which she would exhibit her paintings, and that she wanted it to spread understanding and acceptance.
claims.speaker: Caroline

claims.text: Melanie took her children to a park on 27 August 2023, where they explored and played outdoors.
claims.speaker: Melanie

claims.text: Caroline volunteered at an LGBTQ+ youth centre before 28 August 2023 and found talking with young people like herself gratifying, saying it reminded her how essential kindness and support are.
claims.speaker: Caroline

claims.text: Caroline said she shared her own story with the young people at the LGBTQ+ youth centre so they would know they are not alone, and found it a powerful and emotional experience that reminded her of her own past isolation.
claims.speaker: Caroline

claims.text: Caroline intended to carry on volunteering at the LGBTQ+ youth centre, saying it is an important part of her life and that she has made strong connections there.
claims.speaker: Caroline

claims.text: On 28 August 2023 Caroline said the youth centre was putting together a talent show for the young people the following month, and that she looked forward to seeing them proud of their talents.
claims.speaker: Caroline

claims.text: Melanie went to an outdoor show by the band Summer Sounds before 28 August 2023, who played a lively pop song that got the crowd dancing and singing; she said it reminded her how music brings people together and that she loves live music.
claims.speaker: Melanie

claims.text: Caroline mainly plays the acoustic guitar, which she took up around 2018, about five years before 28 August 2023, and she says playing and singing let her express herself, get her emotions out and connect with others.
claims.speaker: Caroline

claims.text: 'Brave' by Sara Bareilles is the song with the most significance for Caroline: she says it is about being courageous and fighting for what is right, and hearing it makes her think of the paths she has taken and the progress she has made.
claims.speaker: Caroline

claims.text: Melanie plays the clarinet, which she started as a child and uses to express herself and relax; she likes both classical music such as Bach and Mozart and modern music such as Ed Sheeran's 'Perfect'.
claims.speaker: Melanie

claims.text: Caroline spent a day out biking with her group of friends over the weekend of 9-10 September 2023 and found it refreshing.
claims.speaker: Caroline

claims.text: Melanie's family went camping a few weeks before 13 September 2023, exploring the forest, hiking, roasting marshmallows and telling stories round the campfire; she said watching the children get excited about nature makes being a parent worth it.
claims.speaker: Melanie

claims.text: Caroline said she is inspired by seeing her work make a difference for the LGBTQ+ community and by the support of her friends, family and mentors, which also keeps her making art.
claims.speaker: Caroline

claims.text: Caroline has been making art since she was about 17, around 2012, and finds it empowering and cathartic because it can show things that are hard to put into words.
claims.speaker: Caroline

claims.text: Melanie has been making art for seven years, since about 2016, and says painting and pottery are her real muses because they are calming and satisfying and serve as both a creative outlet and a form of therapy.
claims.speaker: Melanie

claims.text: Caroline said painting and drawing helped her express her feelings and explore her gender identity, and that making art was important to her during her transition because it helped her understand and accept herself.
claims.speaker: Caroline

claims.text: As of 13 September 2023 Caroline had still not tried pottery but said she was game to try it sometime.
claims.speaker: Caroline

claims.text: Caroline painted a red and blue piece about her path as a trans woman, the two colours standing for the binary gender system and their mixing for breaking that rigid thinking; she said it reminds her to love her authentic self and that she is finally proud of who she is.
claims.speaker: Caroline

claims.text: Caroline said her transition changed her relationships: some close friends kept supporting her while a few could not handle it, and she is happier among people who accept and love her, so her relationships now feel more genuine.
claims.speaker: Caroline

claims.text: Melanie had a good time at a café over the weekend of 9-10 September 2023 and photographed a sign there which, she told Caroline, was only a precaution.
claims.speaker: Melanie

claims.text: Caroline contacted her mentor for adoption advice on 13 October 2023, saying she is ready to be a mother and to share her love and her family.
claims.speaker: Caroline

claims.text: A friend of Melanie's adopted a child in 2022; Melanie said the process was long but that they are now very happy with their new child, and it made her wonder about adopting herself.
claims.speaker: Melanie

claims.text: Caroline advised Melanie to research and find an adoption agency or lawyer, gather references, financial information and medical checks, and prepare emotionally because the wait can be hard.
claims.speaker: Caroline

claims.text: Melanie was hurt in September 2023 and had to take a break from pottery, which she uses for self-expression and peace; she kept busy reading a book Caroline had recommended and painting.
claims.speaker: Melanie

claims.text: Melanie painted a pink sunset in the week before 13 October 2023 because she found the colours calming.
claims.speaker: Melanie

claims.text: Caroline had been trying abstract painting as of 13 October 2023, finding it freeing to put her feelings on the canvas without much of a plan.
claims.speaker: Caroline

claims.text: Melanie made an abstract painting with peaceful blue streaks to convey tranquillity, saying blue calms her and she wanted a serene feel with vibrant colours.
claims.speaker: Melanie

claims.text: Caroline went to a transgender poetry reading on 6 October 2023 where transgender people shared their stories through poetry; she called it a safe place for self-expression, empowering, and charged with energy and support.
claims.speaker: Caroline

claims.text: The transgender poetry reading of 6 October 2023 inspired Caroline to draw a woman in a dress, standing for freedom and being real, which she says reminds her to stay true to herself and embrace her womanhood.
claims.speaker: Caroline

claims.text: Melanie's family took a road trip over the weekend of 14-15 October 2023 during which her son was in an accident; he was unhurt, and she described the trip's start as frightening.
claims.speaker: Melanie

claims.text: Melanie said the accident on the road trip of 14-15 October 2023 reminded her that life is precious and made her think about how much she needs her family.
claims.speaker: Melanie

claims.text: Melanie's children enjoyed the Grand Canyon during the family road trip of 14-15 October 2023.
claims.speaker: Melanie

claims.text: Melanie said her other children were scared by their brother's accident but were reassured that he would be all right, and that they are tough and resilient and give her the strength to keep going.
claims.speaker: Melanie

claims.text: Melanie said on 20 October 2023 that her family are her biggest motivation and support and that having them around makes hard times easier.
claims.speaker: Melanie

claims.text: Melanie walked a trail with her children on 19 October 2023 as a way to relax after the road trip, and the children loved it.
claims.speaker: Melanie

claims.text: Melanie said she loves camping with her family because it lets them be present together, bonding over stories, campfires and nature, and because waking to birdsong and fresh air refreshes her.
claims.speaker: Melanie

claims.text: Caroline passed the adoption agency interviews on 20 October 2023 and called it a big move towards her goal of having a family.
claims.speaker: Caroline

claims.text: Melanie bought a pair of wooden figurines on 21 October 2023 that remind her of family love.
claims.speaker: Melanie

claims.text: Caroline said her vision is to build her own family and give a home to children who have never had one, and that adoption is her way of giving back and showing love and acceptance.
claims.speaker: Caroline

claims.text: Caroline said finding self-acceptance was a long process and that she is now ready to offer love and support to those who need it.
claims.speaker: Caroline

claims.text: Caroline said transitioning and reaching acceptance were both hard, and that the help of friends, family and people she looked up to was invaluable in getting her through and helping her find out who she really is.
claims.speaker: Caroline

claims.text: Caroline said on 22 October 2023 that the encouragement of those close to her made her who she is, and that living honestly and being yourself is freeing.
claims.speaker: Caroline

claims.text: Caroline's adoption progressed through 2023 from researching LGBTQ-friendly agencies in May, through an adoption council meeting on 14 July and an application to agencies in the week to 23 August, to passing the agency interviews on 20 October 2023.
claims.speaker: Caroline

claims.text: Melanie's pottery went from signing up for a class on 2 July 2023, through a bowl she made there and a workshop she took her children to on 14 July, to a plate made on 24 August 2023, and then stopped when an injury in September 2023 forced her to take a break.
claims.speaker: Melanie

claims.text: Caroline's involvement with the LGBTQ community deepened through 2023, from attending a support group on 7 May and speaking at a school in early June, to joining a youth mentorship programme on the weekend of 15-16 July, the activist group Connected LGBTQ Activists on 18 July, and volunteering at an LGBTQ+ youth centre by late August 2023.
claims.speaker: Caroline
